version.changelog: v1.3.0 — the player itself, to paste. Three lines of HTML run the LYGO TV Ninja player on any site: Rumble room first, ~12,000 channels pulled cross-origin from chatagent.ca/sources/catalog.json, Prev/Next, Sound, branded bar linking home. Ships embed/lygo-tv-embed.html (a whole branded page), vendored lygo-tv-ninja.js/.css for self-hosting, a new 'embed' command, and a self-check that reads the version from SKILL.md instead of hardcoding it. The pointer contract is unchanged: nothing in this package fetches anything.

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent TV-player/embed helper, but the recommended widget runs mutable remote code and channel data in visitors' browsers with weak validation and a documented terms-gate mismatch, so it belongs in Review.

dimensions.detail: For a TV widget, browser network access and media iframes are expected, but automatically ingesting thousands of mutable remote catalog/playlist entries and assigning catalog-influenced URLs into an unsandboxed iframe is not proportionately constrained.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The local Python scripts appear limited to printing URLs/snippets, but the documented website integration hot-links remote JavaScript from chatagent.ca without SRI or immutable pinning, allowing behavior to change after review. The install examples also use unpinned npx clawhub@latest.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The agent instructions tell agents to paste the hosted three-line embed for broad TV/widget requests. The docs say FAST/world lists appear after a Terms tick, while the shipped player says 'No terms gate' and starts catalog and playlist loading automatically.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No local persistence, privilege escalation, filesystem writes, subprocess use, or background workers were found in the skill scripts. Browser localStorage is used only for the sound preference, but embedding sites take on continuing dependence on mutable hosted assets and catalog data.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The purpose is clear: point users to LYGO TV or provide an embeddable TV player. However, the shipped player fetches a live remote catalog, additional playlist URLs, and a third-party HLS library, then uses remote channel metadata to drive iframe/video playback; that is broader and higher-impact than a simple pointer or snippet printer.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing or embedding, treat this as third-party active web code, not just documentation. Use the hosted widget only on sites where you accept chatagent.ca changing the script/catalog later, visitor browsers contacting that service and playlist hosts, and the current iframe validation weakness. Prefer self-hosting reviewed assets, adding CSP/sandbox controls, and pinning installer/tool versions where possible.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The distinction between local scripts and browser-executed embed code is partly disclosed in SKILL.md and SECURITY.md, but the remote active-content behavior is high-impact and not fully bounded.
[P2] expected: The flagged HTML comment is branding/source metadata, not an instruction to the agent; I did not treat it as prompt injection.
[SDI-1] expected: Remote catalog and playlist fetching is core to the player and is disclosed, but the mutable feed materially changes runtime behavior after review.
[SQP-2] expected: Embedding hosted JavaScript is expected for the advertised widget, but the package does not provide SRI, immutable asset pinning, or a strong privacy/integrity warning for visitor-browser requests.
[RP1] unexpected: The repeated npx clawhub@latest examples are an avoidable supply-chain risk; this is a review note rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[LP3] unexpected: The artifact does declare permissions in SKILL.md and claw.json, so the scanner concern is downgraded.
[SQP-1] expected: The activation text is broad but aligned with a TV-player skill; concern comes from steering generic requests toward a high-impact third-party embed.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The player header and behavior omit a terms gate while the documentation describes one for public lists, creating a real disclosure/control mismatch.
[SDI-2] expected: Large playlist ingestion fits the IPTV/player purpose, but the scale and mutable remote sources increase the attack surface.
[T09] unexpected: I accepted the static finding in substance: catalog-provided live entries can preserve a supplied kind, be marked https, and later influence an unsandboxed iframe src without strict scheme/host validation.
